john_cust: Hey team — starting ~10:05 UTC we're seeing waves of 429s for tenant t-42 across multiple microservices. Not a single endpoint: looks like our worker fanouts are triggering rate limits downstream.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this, John. Can you share a short sample of the failing request (curl or SDK) and any 'x-rate' or Retry-After headers you're seeing?

john_cust: pasted logs: 
```
2026-02-15T10:05:12Z ERROR request failed id=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/generate hdrs={"X-RateLimit-Limit":"600","X-RateLimit-Remaining":"0","Retry-After":"30"}
2026-02-15T10:05:12Z ERROR request failed id=abc124 status=429 route=/v1/embeddings hdrs={"X-RateLimit-Limit":"300","X-RateLimit-Remaining":"0","Retry-After":"60"}
```
We have a job that fans out -> seq of 20 downstream calls per high-level transaction. We test-reproduced with a simple loop, see same 429 pattern.

devin_sre: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: (1) per-key RPM is exhausted due to aggregate fanout, (2) per-route TPM (tokens per minute) or burst window is triggering at the edge proxy. Which SDK / auth token are you using — a single shared API key for all downstream calls?

john_cust: Yes, one shared API key used by the worker pool. Concurrency ~12, each transaction does ~20 calls so bursts of ~240 requests in a few seconds.

alex_engineer: That's the typical ‘fanout with shared key’ pattern. The platform counts requests against the API key, so 240 quick requests will drain your RPM quota and immediately hit 429s. Two short fixes: (A) reduce parallelism/shape bursts (client-side queueing or token bucket), (B) batch calls where possible (we have a /batch embeddings endpoint).

maria_support: For troubleshooting: can you run this quick repro and paste the exact curl + response headers? Example repro we use locally: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 240); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
It should show many 200s followed by 429s with Retry-After.

john_cust: ran it. Sample response headers from last failed call: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Window: minute
Retry-After: 34
X-Redwood-RateScope: key
```

devin_sre: Good, that confirms per-key window enforcement. Short-term mitigation options: (1) implement exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s (clients should honor Retry-After); (2) shard traffic across multiple API keys if your flow can partition tenants; (3) request a temporary quota bump — we can raise RPM for t-42 while you refactor.

alex_engineer: Also check for hidden retries inside your stack (retries + concurrency amplify the fanout). If you have an upstream queue that retries on errors immediately, that will thrash the rate window. Add retry-with-jitter and do not retry on 429 except after honoring Retry-After.

john_cust: We do have a retry middleware that retries 3x with 200ms backoff — sounds like that's the culprit. We'll disable retries for 429s and implement exponential backoff.

maria_support: I'll open a ticket to evaluate a temporary RPM increase for tenant t-42 while you deploy changes. Devin — can you check logs for any edge proxy 429-ratecode tags for this key?

devin_sre: On it. Searching... found repeated entries: 
```
edge-proxy[proxy-7] rate_limit.cc:214 WARN key=t-42 code=RATE_WINDOW_EXHAUSTED window=minute count=605 limit=600
edge-proxy[proxy-7] fallback.cc:98 INFO key=t-42 fallback=enabled reason=rate_exhaust
```
So they hit the minute window and then dropped into fallback. We can approve a +50% minute bump for 24h while they fix backoff.

john_cust: That would be great, thanks. Timeline — we'll disable immediate retries and roll a backoff patch in next 30m, then test.

alex_engineer: Additional longer-term suggestions: (a) per-tenant pooling of downstream calls — reuse a shared batcher so you only send one request per 20 logical ops, (b) use dedicated capacity if you need predictable high throughput, (c) instrument request-ids and latency histograms to detect burst hotspots.

maria_support: John — we've created support ticket #SUP-4521 and requested the +50% minute quota for t-42 for 24 hours. You'll get an email when it's applied. Please confirm after your patch. :thumbsup:

john_cust: Confirmed — saw the quota bump in headers almost immediately (X-RateLimit-Limit: 900). Patch deployed, retries disabled, backoff added, running the same loop now. First pass looks clean, only a few 429s during the transition and they respect Retry-After now. We'll do batching next. Thanks all.

ops-bot: NOTE: Temporary quota change applied to t-42 by ops; reason: customer remediation; expires 2026-02-16T10:05:00Z.

maria_support: Great — re-open if anything flares. Closing thread unless you need follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
